title: Lesson 10: Your Calling - Putting It All Together
description: You were made for more than a seat in the crowd. This final lesson of Growing Out brings together everything you have learned and helps you see where God has shaped you to serve.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you saw who God puts beside you in His mission, from your own church to the ends of the earth. Now the question gets personal: where do you fit?

blocks.title: A Place for Every Part
blocks.text:
Imagine a body trying to walk with only one foot doing all the work. Or a hand deciding it has no value because it cannot see. Paul used this picture to describe the church. Some believers felt unimportant; others acted as though they needed no one. Paul answered that God arranged the parts of the body as He chose, and every part matters (1 Corinthians 12:14-27).

A hand does not have to become an eye to be useful. It belongs to the body and serves alongside the other parts. In the same way, God gives His people different gifts so they can care for one another and build up the church. The question is not whether you have the most visible role. It is how you can love and serve the people God has placed around you.

You may wonder where you fit or whether you have anything important to offer. Scripture begins with a better question: you belong to Christ and to His people. God does not ask every believer to do the same work. He calls each person to love and serve as part of His body.
10.1 - When have you felt that your contribution was too small to matter, and what does Paul's picture of the body say to that fear?
Called First to Jesus
Before calling is about a role, it is about a Person. Paul wrote:

I therefore, a prisoner for the Lord, urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling to which you have been called, with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, eager to maintain the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

Your first calling is to follow Jesus, and every other calling grows out of that one. You were saved by grace, not by your work, and yet you were "created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand" (Ephesians 2:10). God has already prepared good works with your name on them. Your part is to walk in them.
Your SHAPE

God's call on your life shows up in how He made you. One simple way to see it is to look at your SHAPE: your spiritual gifts, your heart, your abilities, your personality, and your experiences. No two people have the same one.

You began discovering your spiritual gifts in the Growing Up course. Your heart is the people or the need that stirs you most. Your abilities are the skills in your hands. Your personality is how God wired you. Your experiences, including the painful ones, can become comfort for someone else. Put them together and you start to see where you fit.
10.2 - Which part of your SHAPE do you see most clearly, and who could help you see the rest?
Putting It All Together
Look back at the road you have walked.

items: In Starting in Discipleship, you heard the good news that saves you and began the first habits of a new life: prayer, the Bible, the church, and a heart that keeps turning back to God.
In Growing Deep, you learned to love God and let your roots go down into Him. You saw that you are clothed in Christ's righteousness, and that grace you receive is meant to keep moving through you.

In Growing Up, you learned to love the people God put beside you: your family, your church, and your neighbors. You discovered your spiritual gifts and learned that covenant love says, I will, even when.

In Growing Out, you learned that you are sent. You drew your Personal Ministry Map, practiced the BLESS rhythms, learned to draw the 3 Circles, stood firm in the armor of God, and saw how to pass your faith on to someone else.

blocks.text: Your calling is where all of it meets: a life rooted in Jesus, loving His people, and sent into the world. None of it was earned. Every step was grace, and the God who began this work in you is still at it.

You may feel unqualified. Moses did. When God called him, his first answer was, "Who am I?" God did not answer by listing Moses' strengths. He said, "But I will be with you" (Exodus 3:11-12). Your calling does not rest on how capable you feel. It rests on the God who goes with you.

Finding your place usually happens by serving, not by waiting. Others often see your SHAPE before you do. As you serve, notice where you come alive and where God seems to bear fruit. Calling becomes clearer as you walk, and you will not serve alone.
10.3 - Where in your church could your SHAPE meet a real need?
Calling Grows Clearer as You Serve

Your SHAPE is a helpful starting point, not a test that reveals a secret plan. Every Christian is called to love God and neighbor, grow in holiness, and serve others. Your opportunities may change through the seasons of life. Ask trusted believers where they see you helping others, pay attention to real needs, and take one faithful step. You do not need to discover a perfect role before you can obey Jesus.
This Week's Practice

Take one step toward a team this week. Ask one person who knows you well, "Where do you see God using me?" Then talk with a pastor or ministry leader about one place where your SHAPE could meet a real need, and offer to serve there for one season. You do not have to find the perfect fit before you begin.
Lesson 10 Review

God has placed every believer in Christ's body, where each part matters and serves the others. Your first calling is to follow Jesus, and your opportunities to serve become clearer as you notice needs, listen to the church, and take faithful steps. Your SHAPE can help you reflect, but Christ and His Word guide your life. Growing Together has been leading toward this: a life rooted in Jesus, loving His people, and bearing fruit for His mission.
This is the last lesson of the 200 series. The next step is the 300 series, Leading in Discipleship, where you will learn to lead others the way you have been led.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
This lesson draws on the SHAPE idea from The Purpose Driven Life by Rick Warren.
